name: ChatGPT
what_it_is: The highest-volume answer surface. It names a handful of sources per answer and almost never shows the runners-up.
the_move: Ask it the question your buyer would actually type, once a month, and write down every company it names. That list is your real competitive set.
watch_out: Answers change from one day to the next, so a single check proves nothing. You need the same questions asked on a schedule.
audit_2026: Still the biggest surface: about 54% of worldwide AI-chat web visits in May 2026 (Similarweb via Momentic), down from roughly 79% a year earlier. Gemini and Claude are taking the share.

name: Perplexity
what_it_is: Citation-first by design — it shows its sources inline, which makes it the cheapest place on earth to check whether you are retrievable.
the_move: Search your own category here first. If nothing of yours comes back, stop writing and go fix retrieval.
watch_out: Tiny share of total AI traffic (about 1 to 2%), so it is a thermometer, not a market. Winning here is a test, not a result.
audit_2026: Still citation-first. Share stayed small through 2026 as the bigger assistants added their own search.

name: Claude
what_it_is: Answers from fewer, longer sources. Rewards a page that holds a full argument over one that covers a keyword.
the_move: Give it one page that answers the whole question end to end instead of five that each answer a fifth.
watch_out: Smaller audience than ChatGPT or Gemini, and it leans on fewer sources, so you are either the source or you are absent.
audit_2026: Fastest-growing major assistant through 2026: roughly 9% of worldwide AI-chat web visits by May 2026, about 13% in the US.

name: AI Overviews
what_it_is: Google's generated answer above the ten blue links. It absorbs the click that used to go to position one.
the_move: Check which queries in your category now trigger an Overview. Those are the pages where ranking alone stopped paying.
watch_out: You cannot opt in. The box appears or it does not, and you only find out by checking the queries yourself.

name: AI Mode
what_it_is: Google's conversational surface. It fans one typed question into many hidden ones and assembles the answer from all of them.
the_move: Write for the follow-up questions, not just the entry question — the fan-out is where most sources get picked up.
watch_out: The hidden questions are never shown to you, so you have to guess at them from your own sales calls and support tickets.

name: Gemini
what_it_is: Google's assistant, and increasingly the default inside Workspace, where a lot of B2B research quietly happens.
the_move: Test your category prompt in a signed-in Workspace account, not an incognito tab — the grounded answer differs.
watch_out: There are two Geminis, the app and the Workspace version, and they can answer differently. You have to test both.
audit_2026: Big change: Apple's Siri AI (announced at WWDC, June 8 2026) is built on Gemini. Roughly 28% of worldwide AI-chat web visits in May 2026, up from about 5% a year earlier.

name: Copilot
what_it_is: Bing-grounded and embedded in Microsoft 365, which means it sits inside the tools enterprise buyers already have open.
the_move: Verify Bing has indexed your site at all. Plenty of sites are fine in Google and invisible in Bing.
watch_out: Small consumer share (about 1 to 3%), and Bing's index lags Google, so fresh pages can take weeks to show up.
audit_2026: Still a small share of consumer visits but embedded in the enterprise suite. Unchanged in kind.

name: Grok
what_it_is: Grounded heavily in live posts, so it reflects what is being said about you right now rather than what your site claims.
the_move: Watch what it says about your company. It is the fastest read on your public reputation as machines see it.
watch_out: Grounded in social posts, so one loud week of criticism can rewrite what it says about you overnight.
audit_2026: Verified Oct 2026: Grok ships in Teslas with the AMD chip (roughly 2021 and newer) since the 2025.26 update; the Summer 2026 update added cabin controls, and Grok Bot plus Connectors went live in-car on Sept 22, 2026. About 2 to 3% of AI-chat web visits, but the only major engine with a car cabin.

name: robots.txt
what_it_is: The gate every crawler checks first. One over-broad disallow line can shut out the exact agents that feed the answer engines.
the_move: List the crawlers you actually depend on and allow them by name before you block anything by default.
watch_out: Allowing every crawler also invites the ones that only scrape. Allow the named ones you want, not a blanket yes.

name: Sitemap
what_it_is: The index of what exists and when it last changed. Without it, discovery depends on links you may not have.
the_move: Confirm every page you want cited is in it, and that lastmod reflects real edits rather than a build timestamp.
watch_out: A sitemap only says 'this exists.' It does not make a page worth citing; it just makes sure the page gets read.

name: llms.txt
what_it_is: A plain-text map of what matters on your site, written for models instead of browsers. Emerging convention, cheap to ship.
the_move: Publish one that points at your definitions, pricing, and proof pages. Treat it as a hint, not a guarantee.
watch_out: Google says it does not use the file for Search, AI Overviews or AI Mode (May 2026 guidance), and most files get no traffic at all. Ship it cheap; expect nothing from Google.
audit_2026: Checked Oct 2026: adoption about 10% of domains; an Ahrefs study of 137,000 sites found 97% of files got zero visits in May 2026. Spec v2 shipped Aug 2026, Chrome's Lighthouse added an agentic-browsing check for it, and OpenAI and Anthropic recommend it for agents. Still a hint, now with a known ceiling.

name: agents.txt
what_it_is: Declares what an agent can do on your site — not merely what it may read. The capability layer above robots.txt.
the_move: Only declare capabilities that genuinely work. A false claim here fails in front of the buyer's agent, not yours.
watch_out: Still an early convention. No major engine has confirmed it reads the file, so do not spend more than an afternoon on it until one does.

name: JSON-LD
what_it_is: Structured data that states the facts of a page in a form no parser has to guess at: product, price, author, organization.
the_move: Start with Organization and Product. Everything else is optional until those two are right.
watch_out: Markup that disagrees with the visible page gets ignored, or flagged. Keep both saying the same thing.

name: Entity
what_it_is: The link between your name and a thing the model already knows about. sameAs references, consistent naming, corroborating profiles.
the_move: Pick one canonical name and spelling, then use it identically everywhere. Ambiguity splits your evidence in half.
watch_out: Slow. Entity signals take quarters to build and quarters to fix, so a rename costs more than it looks.

name: Chunk
what_it_is: Retrieval quotes passages, not pages. A paragraph that only makes sense after reading the three above it will not be quoted.
the_move: Make every section survive being torn out of the page. Restate the subject instead of writing 'it' and 'this'.
watch_out: Restating the subject everywhere reads clunky to a human. Do it in the first sentence of each section, not every sentence.

name: Server render
what_it_is: Content present in the HTML response rather than assembled later by JavaScript. Many crawlers never run the script.
the_move: View source — literally. If your key claim is not in the raw HTML, assume no engine has ever read it.
watch_out: Server rendering can slow a dev team's workflow. Render the pages you want cited; leave the app screens alone.

name: Freshness
what_it_is: A visible, accurate date. Models weigh recency heavily on anything that looks like it could be stale.
the_move: Put a real published-and-updated date on every substantive page, and only bump it when the content changed.
watch_out: Fake freshness backfires. Only bump the date when the content actually changed.

name: Canonical
what_it_is: The single address a piece of content lives at. Split versions divide the signal between them and neither wins.
the_move: Point every duplicate and syndicated copy at one canonical URL before you build more links to any of them.
watch_out: Pointing everything at one URL means that one URL has to be the best version. Fix it before you consolidate.

name: Transcript
what_it_is: A video is citable only to the extent its words exist somewhere as text. The file itself is opaque.
the_move: Publish the transcript on a real page. This is why engines cite YouTube and never cite a raw video file.
watch_out: Raw auto-captions are full of errors. A wrong product name in a transcript can get quoted exactly as written.

name: Alt text
what_it_is: The only description of an image most retrieval pipelines will ever have. Chart, screenshot, diagram — all invisible without it.
the_move: Describe what the image proves, not what it depicts. 'Bar chart' says nothing; the finding says everything.
watch_out: Stuffing keywords into alt text reads as spam and hurts screen-reader users. Describe the finding, once.

name: Heading map
what_it_is: The outline a parser builds from your H2s and H3s. It decides where one idea stops and the next begins.
the_move: Make every heading a claim or a question, never a label like 'Overview'. Labels carry no retrievable meaning.
watch_out: Question-shaped headings get long. Keep them under ten words or they stop reading as headings.

name: Internal links
what_it_is: How crawlers find the page and how models infer what it is about from the words pointing at it.
the_move: Link to the page using the words you want to be found for. Kill every 'click here' and 'learn more'.
watch_out: The same anchor text everywhere reads as manipulation. Use the natural phrase, not one phrase fifty times.

name: Clarity
what_it_is: Whether the first line says what the thing is in words a stranger already knows.
the_move: Delete the first sentence and check whether anything was lost. Usually it was throat-clearing.
watch_out: Clear can sound plain. That is fine. Plain gets quoted; clever gets skipped.

name: Specificity
what_it_is: Named nouns beat adjectives. A sentence with a number, a unit, and a named thing in it is quotable; one without is not.
the_move: Rewrite your strongest claim until it contains a figure, a unit, and the condition it holds under.
watch_out: A specific claim can be checked and can be wrong. Only publish numbers you can defend when a buyer asks.

name: Proof
what_it_is: A claim with a source, a number, and a date attached. Models reproduce claims they can attribute.
the_move: For every number on the page, add where it came from and when. Unsourced numbers get dropped, not repeated.
watch_out: Proof dates. A number from 2023 with no update starts to count against you.

name: Buyer outcome
what_it_is: The changed state the buyer ends up in, stated in their language rather than your feature list.
the_move: Name the outcome and what it currently costs them. Features answer 'what is it', outcomes answer 'why now'.
watch_out: Outcomes you cannot measure turn into vague claims. Pair each outcome with a number or leave it out.

name: Comparison
what_it_is: An honest account of how you differ from the named alternatives. Buyers ask engines to compare constantly.
the_move: Write the comparison yourself, fairly. If you don't, a review site writes it for you and gets cited instead.
watch_out: Comparisons go stale fast when competitors change pricing or features. Date them and revisit every quarter.

name: Pricing clarity
what_it_is: A number, a unit, and what changes it. 'Contact us' removes you from every price-shaped question.
the_move: Publish a starting price and the dimension it scales on. You can still qualify the deal on the call.
watch_out: A public price anchors every negotiation. Publish the starting point and the scaling dimension, not the whole sheet.

name: Rich media
what_it_is: Whether your video and images are citable or opaque. A player an agent cannot read scores as absent.
the_move: Host video where the words are indexable and link it. A native player with no transcript is a blank space.
watch_out: Hosting on YouTube means YouTube gets some of the credit. Worth it; just link back hard.

name: FAQ block
what_it_is: Question-shaped headings with self-contained answers — the exact shape retrieval wants to lift.
the_move: Use your real support tickets as the question list. Invented questions match no one's actual query.
watch_out: A 40-question FAQ dilutes the page. Ten real questions beat forty invented ones.

name: Definition
what_it_is: A crisp 'X is Y' sentence near the top. Definitional queries are the highest-volume door into any category.
the_move: Define the term in one sentence before you explain anything. Models quote definitions almost verbatim.
watch_out: If your definition disagrees with the common one, you get skipped, not corrected. Define the term the way the world does, then add your angle.

name: Teardown
what_it_is: A public, specific critique of a real example. Reliably the most-shared artifact in a technical niche.
the_move: Tear down something you did not make, name it, and be fair. Cheap to produce, hard to ignore.
watch_out: Naming competitors invites them to respond. Be accurate enough that you would be fine with them reading it.

name: Benchmark
what_it_is: A number nobody else has because nobody else measured it. The single most citable object you can publish.
the_move: Measure something in your niche at n greater than fifty, publish the method, and repeat it on a schedule.
watch_out: Takes a quarter to produce and a quarter to get noticed. Slowest element on the table, and the most durable.

name: Dataset
what_it_is: The raw rows behind a benchmark. It gets referenced long after the post that announced it is forgotten.
the_move: Publish the data at a stable URL with a license. A benchmark you cannot check is a claim, not a source.
watch_out: Publishing data means people can find your mistakes. Check it twice and version it.

name: Case study
what_it_is: One customer, one measured before and after. The proof artifact buyers and models both look for by name.
the_move: Lead with the number and the timeframe. Company logos are not evidence of anything.
watch_out: Customers have to approve it, and some will not. Get permission for the number, not just the logo.

name: Runbook
what_it_is: Ordered steps someone can follow without you. High utility, high save rate, endlessly quotable.
the_move: Write the one you already run internally. The version you use is better than the version you would write.
watch_out: A runbook that goes stale is worse than none, because people follow the wrong step. Date it and own it.

name: Calculator
what_it_is: An interactive tool that returns a personal number. It earns links from people who will never read your posts.
the_move: Make it answer one question exactly, with no signup. Gating it converts a linkable asset into a form.
watch_out: Takes real build time, and a wrong formula gets screenshotted. Test the math before it ships.

name: Screenshot
what_it_is: Visual evidence the thing exists and works. The cheapest media that materially raises trust.
the_move: Show the real screen with real data, cropped tight. Mockups read as mockups to everyone.
watch_out: Real screens leak real data. Blur what you must; never fake the rest.

name: Video
what_it_is: Highest-trust format on every channel, and the only one that carries tone. Worthless to retrieval without its text.
the_move: Ship it with a transcript and a description written for search, not a one-line caption.
watch_out: Expensive to redo. If a feature changes, the video is wrong until you re-shoot.

name: Newsletter
what_it_is: The one audience nobody can take away — no ranking, no algorithm, no platform between you and the reader.
the_move: Send the same substance you publish. A newsletter that only announces posts teaches people to ignore it.
watch_out: Slow to grow and easy to neglect. Missing issues costs more than never starting.

name: Template
what_it_is: A file someone can open and use today. It converts a reader into a user before any purchase exists.
the_move: Give away the artifact you would normally deliver in week one. It qualifies buyers faster than a demo.
watch_out: A template can look like the whole product. Make sure the paid thing is clearly more.

name: LinkedIn
what_it_is: Graph-gated: reach comes from who already follows you, not from what people search. Documents outperform text.
the_move: Post the artifact as a document carousel. Text-only posts on this surface travel roughly nowhere.
watch_out: Almost nothing posted here gets cited by answer engines. It is a reach channel, not a retrieval channel.

name: YouTube
what_it_is: Query-gated, so it compounds instead of decaying — and it is consistently among the most-cited domains in AI answers.
the_move: Title for the question people type. This is the one channel where a video keeps earning years later.
watch_out: Slowest payoff on the table. Months to build, years to earn.

name: Threads
what_it_is: Fast-moving, conversation-shaped, low production cost. Good for testing a claim before you build around it.
the_move: Post the sharpest line from a longer piece and see whether anyone argues. Free positioning research.
watch_out: Fast-moving and barely cited. Treat it as research, not distribution.

name: Reddit
what_it_is: Disproportionately cited by answer engines because the discussion is real. Also the fastest place to get punished for marketing.
the_move: Answer questions in your category as a practitioner for a month before you ever link to anything.
watch_out: Zero tolerance for marketing. One wrong move and you are out, with the thread preserved forever.

name: GitHub
what_it_is: A trusted domain where a README is a document engines read closely. Underused by non-developer companies.
the_move: Publish your dataset, schema, or template as a repo with a real README.
watch_out: Needs upkeep. An abandoned repo with open issues signals an abandoned company.

name: Marketplace
what_it_is: A cloud marketplace listing — an authoritative third-party page describing your product that you mostly control.
the_move: Treat the listing as a landing page, not a form. Same clarity, proof, and pricing rules apply.
watch_out: Platform rules limit what you can say and how. Work inside them; do not fight them.

name: Podcast
what_it_is: Borrowed audience plus a transcript on someone else's trusted domain. Two assets from one hour.
the_move: Ask the host to publish the transcript. That page, not the audio, is what gets cited.
watch_out: No transcript, no retrieval value, and most hosts will not publish one unless asked.

name: Directory
what_it_is: Review and category sites. Engines lean on them heavily for comparison and shortlist questions.
the_move: Fill the profile out completely and get the first few reviews. Empty profiles read as an inactive vendor.
watch_out: Review sites sell placement, and engines sometimes cite the paid lists. You are competing with budgets, not just quality.

name: Instagram
what_it_is: Where the person behind the company becomes legible. Weak for retrieval, strong for recognition.
the_move: Repurpose an existing carousel rather than making anything new. Near-zero cost, real coverage gain.
watch_out: Almost never cited. Do not make anything new for it.

name: Guest post
what_it_is: Your argument on a domain with authority you have not earned yet. Slow, but it moves the entity signal.
the_move: Pitch the specific claim you can prove, not a topic. Editors accept evidence, not subject areas.
watch_out: Quarters, not weeks. And the host site gets the citation, not you, so plan for the link back.

name: Share of voice
what_it_is: Of all answers to your category's questions, the share that names you. The closest thing to a scoreboard.
the_move: Fix the prompt set first. A share-of-voice number over a shifting prompt list measures nothing.
watch_out: Engines vary run to run. One check is noise; a trend across months is signal.
unit: Percent of prompts in which you are named: named ÷ total prompts × 100.
direction: Higher is better. 20% means named in 6 of 30.
alternates: Share of citations (your citations ÷ all citations in the answers), average list position when named (lower is better), or volume-weighted share if some prompts matter more.

name: Mentions
what_it_is: How often you are named at all, cited or not. Being named without a link still shapes the buyer.
the_move: Track named-but-unlinked separately. It is usually your earliest sign that something started working.
watch_out: Easy to inflate with a loud week on social. Watch the trend, not the spike.
unit: Count per period: how many answers named you across the frozen prompt set this month, or mention rate as a percent of prompts.
direction: Higher is better, with one check: a mention can be negative. Tag each one positive, neutral or negative.
alternates: Named-but-unlinked vs linked (track separately), mention rate per prompt, or sentiment-split counts.

name: Citations
what_it_is: Answers that link you as a source. The strongest evidence a specific page earned its place.
the_move: Track which page gets cited, not just that you were. One page usually carries the whole result.
watch_out: Citations do not equal clicks. Many answers get read and never clicked.
unit: Count per period: answers that link to your domain as a source, or citation rate as cited answers ÷ prompts.
alternates: Unique cited URLs (how many different pages earn citations), citation share (yours ÷ all citations), or position of your link in the source list.

name: Prompt set
what_it_is: The fixed list of questions you re-ask on a schedule. Without it, every other number here drifts.
the_move: Write thirty real buyer questions, freeze them, date the file, and change it only on purpose.
watch_out: Real questions are boring and specific. Resist the urge to add the ones you wish buyers asked.
unit: Not a metric; the ruler. Its unit is a count of prompts (30) and a version date.
direction: Stable is good. Changes between periods should be zero unless deliberate, and every change gets a date.
alternates: Coverage: percent of buyer-journey stages or real sales-call questions the set represents. Prompt volume weighting if you have search data.

name: Switchback
what_it_is: Turning a change on and off in alternating time windows. The only clean test when you cannot split traffic by visitor.
the_move: Run windows long enough to clear the crawl cycle. A week is usually the floor.
watch_out: Slow and fiddly. Only worth running on changes big enough to matter.
unit: Lift in percentage points: citation rate in on-weeks minus citation rate in off-weeks.
direction: Higher positive is better. Near zero means the change didn't matter. Negative means undo it.
alternates: Ratio (on ÷ off), raw citation count delta. Minimum one week per block and at least two on/off cycles before you believe it.

name: AI referrals
what_it_is: Sessions arriving from an answer engine. Small in volume, and consistently the highest-intent traffic on the site.
the_move: Segment them out. Judged against organic averages they look like a rounding error instead of your best cohort.
watch_out: Attribution is leaky. Many AI visits arrive as 'direct' and never get counted.
unit: Sessions per period from AI referrers (chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com, copilot.microsoft.com and the rest), and that segment's conversion rate as a percent.
direction: Higher is better on both. Expect under 2% of sessions; the proof is the conversion rate running several times organic.
alternates: Share of total sessions, assisted conversions, revenue per AI session. Many AI visits arrive as 'direct' and are not counted here.

name: Brand search
what_it_is: People searching your name directly. It rises when awareness works, whatever the attribution says.
the_move: Watch branded query volume as the lagging check on every campaign that promised awareness.
watch_out: Lags by months, and it cannot tell you which effort caused the rise.
unit: Branded search impressions and clicks per month from Search Console, or a Google Trends index from 0 to 100.
direction: Higher is better, and it lags everything else by weeks to months.
alternates: Count of distinct branded queries, direct traffic as a proxy, or brand-name mention volume across the web.

name: Impressions
what_it_is: How many times you were shown. Necessary context, and worthless as a goal on its own.
the_move: Only ever read it next to a downstream number. Alone it rewards volume over reach that matters.
watch_out: Rewards volume over relevance. Chasing it alone makes slop.
unit: Count: times you were shown, as Search Console impressions or an AI-tracking tool's appearances.
direction: Neutral on its own. Read it only as a ratio: citations per 100 impressions. 10,000 impressions and 2 citations is a problem; 500 and 40 is a win.
alternates: Impression share within your prompt set, or citations ÷ impressions as the one number worth watching.

name: Blocked crawler
what_it_is: A disallow rule aimed at scrapers that also shuts out the agents feeding the engines you want to appear in.
the_move: Audit robots.txt line by line. This is the highest-cost, lowest-effort mistake on the whole table.
watch_out: Unblocking everything lets the scrapers back in. Allow by name.

name: JS-only
what_it_is: Content that only exists after the script runs. Many retrieval pipelines never get that far.
the_move: Server-render anything you want quoted. Everything else can stay client-side.
watch_out: Fixing it can mean a rebuild. Prioritize the five pages that matter.

name: Gated
what_it_is: Your best evidence sitting behind a form. Invisible to every engine and most buyers.
the_move: Ungate the proof and gate the tailored thing instead — the audit, the walkthrough, the custom number.
watch_out: Sales teams like the form. Show them the citation count before you take it away.

name: Paywall
what_it_is: Same failure as a gate, with a card attached. The content may be excellent and it cannot be cited.
the_move: Leave the definition, the method, and the headline number outside the wall.
watch_out: Giving away the headline number can feel like giving away the product. It is not. It is the ad.

name: Jargon wall
what_it_is: Language only an insider parses. It fails both the model matching intent and the buyer scanning for fit.
the_move: Read the first paragraph aloud to someone outside your category. Rewrite whatever they ask about.
watch_out: Some jargon is the search term. Keep the term, explain it in the next sentence.

name: Vague claim
what_it_is: 'Industry-leading', 'seamless', 'enterprise-grade'. Unfalsifiable, so unquotable — nothing to attribute.
the_move: Replace each one with a number and a source, or delete the sentence entirely.
watch_out: Deleting them shrinks the page. Good. That is the point.

name: Duplicate
what_it_is: The same content at several addresses, splitting whatever authority any single version might have had.
the_move: Pick the canonical URL and point everything else at it, including the syndicated copies.
watch_out: Consolidating can drop traffic briefly while engines re-learn. It recovers; hold steady.

name: Orphan page
what_it_is: A page nothing links to. It exists, and for discovery purposes it does not.
the_move: Run a crawl and link every orphan from somewhere real, or delete it.
watch_out: Linking junk pages makes them discoverable. Delete first, link second.

name: Slop
what_it_is: High-volume thin content. It buries your own good pages and trains readers that your name means noise.
the_move: Cut the volume and raise the floor. Publishable is a bar, not a synonym for finished.
watch_out: Takes a quarter for engines to re-trust a domain after a slop phase. Deleting is faster than waiting.

name: No date
what_it_is: Undated content reads as possibly stale, and stale gets skipped on anything time-sensitive.
the_move: Add a published and updated date sitewide. It is a template change, not a content project.
watch_out: Adding dates exposes how old some pages are. Update or prune the worst ones.
